data.reason: The fifth review returned verdict pass with two medium findings, F9 and F10, both overclaims in prose this ticket itself wrote: the Outcome's opening paragraph still said the fifth criterion blocked the ticket at review, and the workflow document's Permissions row still sent a reader to a criterion SEEN-106 no longer has. Both are fixed. The fix changed the tree, and a review that changed the tree is a review to throw away, so this returns to tdd rather than advancing on a fingerprint the reviewer never read: the regression is re-run against the corrected tree and the review round starts again. Recorded as rework because that is what it is.

findings.claim: The Outcome section's opening summary is stale: it says the fifth criterion still blocks this ticket at review, contradicting the same section's later text and the Amendments section, both of which say the criterion moved to SEEN-110 and this ticket no longer claims it.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader, or a future gate-writing session, reads only the Outcome's first paragraph, sees 'the fifth needs a live Codex session and is the reason this ticket is still at review', and concludes SEEN-106 cannot be done until a Codex session runs against it, when all four of its remaining criteria are checked and proven and the Codex session is SEEN-110's. This is the overclaim-by-omission the reviewer was asked to rule out: the ticket did not consistently claim only what it proves.
findings.resolution: The opening paragraph now says five attempts, all four criteria met, and that the fifth criterion is SEEN-110's by the amendment below so this ticket neither claims it nor waits on it. Fixed in the commit before regression check 57.

findings.claim: The Permissions row still attributes the .agents/settings.json verification to SEEN-106's fifth criterion, a criterion the amendment removed from this ticket and moved unchanged to SEEN-110.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader follows the workflow document's own cross-reference into SEEN-106 to find what settles the .agents/settings.json question, finds no fifth criterion there at all because it was deleted from the ticket file, and has no path from that row to SEEN-110, where the criterion now lives as its second.
findings.resolution: The row now reads 'which is SEEN-110's second criterion, moved there when SEEN-106 was split'. Fixed in the same commit.
